text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"The American Heart Association statement says caffeinated coffee may benefit heart health.","cited_pids":["d490f254eb76#2"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"Coffee lowers atrial fibrillation risk while raising premature ventricular contractions.","cited_pids":["9de9c10251c1#0"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"Moderate caffeine intake is associated with lower stroke risk.","cited_pids":["9de9c10251c1#0"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"In the randomized DECAF trial, drinking about one cup of caffeinated coffee daily was linked to less atrial fibrillation recurrence than abstinence.","cited_pids":["7591d78c5ea0#4"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"Harvard Health notes that only heavy coffee intake, above five or six cups a day, was once thought to harm the heart.","cited_pids":["1e5642249056#1"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"A reanalysis of the DECAF trial questioned whether its statistically significant result was robust.","cited_pids":["e3cc200edfc8#0"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"Many doctors advise palpitation patients to cut back on coffee, and caffeine was a trigger for many atrial fibrillation patients.","cited_pids":["1ffb0bf0641c#6"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"Energy drinks with large caffeine doses are linked to cardiovascular harm.","cited_pids":["d490f254eb76#2"]},{"cid":"c9","text":"Moderate coffee intake appears generally benign or beneficial for the heart, though evidence is mixed.","cited_pids":[]}]}
